messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 76 years
Gender: Male

Hospital Course:
The patient presented with a metachronous cancer in the sigmoid colon during surveillance colonoscopy after a previous right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the colon. He had undergone a second laparotomy with revision of the anastomosis due to an anastomotic leak during the immediate postoperative period. During the first postoperative week, the patient developed an enterocutaneous fistula with primary wound failure.

After subsequent management for the non-surgical healing of the fistula for 10 months, the patient underwent an abdominal wall reconstruction with an inlay polypropylene/polyglactin 910 composite mesh that was fixed using polypropylene sutures. The patient remained asymptomatic for 16 months after the primary surgery, after which he was diagnosed with a sigmoid cancer during surveillance colonoscopy.

At surgery, the patient underwent subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis. Several loops of bowel were tightly adherent to the anterior abdominal wall. After separating the loops from the posterior rectus sheath, an enterotomy was made to extract the heavily deposited mesh from inside the bowel lumen. There were no signs of an abscess, fistula, or sinus formation in the surrounding area.

Post-surgery, the patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged in a stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
- Subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis
- Abdominal wall reconstruction with polypropylene/polyglactin 910 composite mesh

Condition at discharge:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.

Follow-up plan:
The patient is advised to continue with follow-up colonoscopies as part of his surveillance protocol.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was chiefly for the metachronous sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma found on surveillance, which was treated by subtotal colectomy. The mesh-related bowel involvement was a finding during that operation rather than the reason for admission. The sigmoid colon malignancy falls in chapter C (neoplasms), category C18 (malignant neoplasm of colon).

CODE: C18
